# Maximum Product of Three Numbers.

@example The two negatives make 48, and with 5 that is 240; the three largest values give only 5 * 3 * 2 = 30.
[-8,3,-6,2,5]
=> 240

@example Every value is negative, and so is every product; -2, -5 and -7, the three nearest zero, give the one nearest zero.
[-7,-2,-5,-9]
=> -70

@example 4 is at two indices, so both copies can be used: 6 * 4 * 4 = 96 beats -2 * -1 * 6 = 12.
[4,-1,6,-2,4]
=> 96

# Three values: the one possible product, negative here.
[2,-3,4]
=> -24

# The smallest answer.
[-1000,-1000,-1000]
=> -1000000000

# Two negatives of large size and the largest value.
[-1000,-999,1,2,1000]
=> 999000000

# All negative: the three nearest zero, not the three of largest size.
[-4,-1000,-2,-999,-7]
=> -56

# Every product of three nonzero values is negative, but one with the zero is 0.
[-6,5,0,4]
=> 0

# The largest value three times.
[9,-5,9,9]
=> 729

# The same values in increasing, decreasing and mixed order.
[-10,-9,1,2,3,8]
=> 720

[8,3,2,1,-9,-10]
=> 720

[1,-9,8,-10,3,2]
=> 720

# 257 copies of -1000, with 999 and 1: a value that occurs more than 255 times.
[-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,999,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,-1000,1]
=> 999000000

=> 1000000000

# Random small cases from gen.c (lc check --regen makes them).
@gen 1 small
[4,1,-5,-5,-3]
=> 100

@gen 2 small
[-998,997,-997,996,998,1000,-996]
=> 995006000

@gen 3 small
[-5,-5,-5,-4,-5,4,-5,-5]
=> 100

@gen 4 small
[-5,5,1,-1]
=> 25

@gen 5 small
[5,3,-4,-2,-3,-5]
=> 100

@gen 6 small
[-1,-3,-5,2,3,0]
=> 45
